name: OSG202 — Luyện tập
description: Bộ luyện môn OSG202 (Operating Systems) bám giáo trình Tanenbaum và đề FE của trường — mỗi bài học một bộ đề từ dễ đến khó, con số trong đề do bộ mô phỏng tính (lập lịch CPU, thay trang, Banker, lập lịch đĩa, cấp phát bộ nhớ, dịch địa chỉ, i-node/FAT, semaphore, race condition); bài khó là viết hàm mô phỏng chạy thật trong trình duyệt; mỗi chương một Lab và đề FE thi thử cuối môn.

modules.name: 1.1 What an OS is: kernel & system calls
modules.description: Luyện: Kernel mode, user mode and the role of the OS · Which operations need kernel mode? · Order the steps of a system call · Match the UNIX system call to its purpose · Summarise a strace log and find leaked descriptors

modules.name: 1.3 Hardware review: interrupts, DMA & dual mode
modules.description: Luyện: Interrupts, traps and the memory hierarchy (concepts) · Average memory access time with a cache · Order the steps of interrupt handling · How much CPU do interrupts cost?

modules.name: 2.2 Threads & parallel speed-up
modules.description: Luyện: What do threads share and what is private? · CPU utilisation with multiprogramming: 1 − pⁿ · Amdahl’s law: speed-up of a parallel program · Pthreads: join, detach and thread-safe code · How many cores do you need? (Amdahl, solved in code)

modules.name: 2.3 Process states, the PCB & fork/exec
modules.description: Luyện: Which transition does the event cause? · fork(), exec(), zombie and orphan · How many processes and how many lines? · Output buffering and wait(): what really gets printed? · Order the life of the command “ls -l” · Write a fork-tree counter

modules.name: 2.4 Scheduling algorithms, calculated
modules.description: Luyện: FCFS: completion, turnaround and waiting time · Which algorithm? (convoy effect, starvation, quantum) · SJF (non-preemptive) versus SRTF (preemptive) · Round Robin (q = 3): the order of the time slices · How the quantum changes Round Robin · Priority scheduling: non-preemptive and preemptive · Write

modules.name: 2.5 IPC & synchronization: races, mutex, semaphore
modules.description: Luyện: Critical sections and the four conditions · The lost update: counter++ without a lock · Trace a counting semaphore · Semaphores that enforce an order · Enumerate every outcome of a data race · Write a semaphore simulator

modules.name: 2.6 The three classical IPC problems
modules.description: Luyện: Producer–consumer: the three semaphores · Order the producer, then spot the deadlock · Readers–writers and the philosophers (concepts) · Dining philosophers: which Coffman condition does each strategy break? · When does the bounded buffer first block? · Simulate the dining philosophers

modules.name: Lab 2 — CPU scheduler comparison report
modules.description: Luyện: CPU scheduler comparison report

modules.name: 3.0 Memory allocation: swapping, holes & fit strategies
modules.description: Luyện: Where does each request go? First, best, worst, next fit · Internal fragmentation of paged processes · The buddy system: block sizes · Swapping, base/limit, compaction · Write a hole allocator

modules.name: 3.1 Paging & virtual memory
modules.description: Luyện: Split a virtual address: offset bits, page-number bits, number of pages · Translate logical addresses with a page table · How big is a single-level page table? · Internal fragmentation, protection and the bits of a PTE · Write an MMU: translate a batch of addresses

modules.name: 3.2 Page faults & replacement
modules.description: Luyện: Count the page faults of FIFO, LRU and OPT · FIFO step by step: hit or fault? · LRU: which page is evicted at each fault? · Belady’s anomaly: more frames, more faults? · Second chance (Clock) versus FIFO · NRU, aging, working set: which is which? · Write a page-replacement simulator

modules.name: 3.3 Address translation: page tables & the TLB
modules.description: Luyện: The path of one memory access (TLB miss, page present) · Effective access time with a TLB · Split a 32-bit address for a two-level page table (10 | 10 | 12) · TLB flushes, ASIDs, inverted page tables · Split an address into n fields and count TLB hits

modules.name: 3.4 Working set, thrashing & frame allocation
modules.description: Luyện: Compute W(t, Δ) · Proportional frame allocation · Recognising and curing thrashing · Working-set sizes over time and the thrashing test

modules.name: Lab 3 — A tiny virtual-memory machine
modules.description: Luyện: A tiny virtual-memory machine (TLB + page table + replacement)

modules.name: 4.1 Files, directories & implementation
modules.description: Luyện: Files, directories and links (concepts) · Follow the FAT chain · Match the allocation method to the property · Walk and validate a FAT chain

modules.name: 4.2 Allocation methods, i-nodes & permissions
modules.description: Luyện: Maximum file size of a UNIX i-node · How many disk reads for one byte? · Permissions in octal, symbolic form and umask · Hard links, symbolic links and what an i-node stores · Size of the free-space bitmap · Locate a byte through the indirect blocks

modules.name: Lab 4 — A mini FAT file system
modules.description: Luyện: A mini FAT file system

modules.name: 5.1 I/O hardware & software
modules.description: Luyện: Polling, interrupts, DMA and memory-mapped I/O · The I/O software stack and a DMA transfer · Disk access time = seek + rotational latency + transfer · RAID: usable capacity and guaranteed fault tolerance · RAID capacity and disk access time in code

modules.name: 5.2 Disk scheduling, calculated
modules.description: Luyện: FCFS and SSTF: service order and total head movement · SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK: total head movement · Order the requests as SSTF serves them · Order the requests as SCAN serves them (moving down first) · Which algorithm for which workload? · Write a disk-scheduling simulator

modules.name: Lab 5 — Disk scheduler with requests arriving over time
modules.description: Luyện: Disk scheduler with requests arriving over time

modules.name: 6.1 Deadlock: conditions & handling
modules.description: Luyện: The four conditions and the ostrich · Read a resource-allocation graph (one instance per resource) · Which condition does each prevention technique attack? · Prevention, avoidance, detection or recovery? · Detect a cycle in a resource-allocation graph

modules.name: 6.2 Resource graphs & the Banker’s algorithm
modules.description: Luyện: Compute the Need matrix · Find the safe sequence · Resource-request decisions · Deadlock detection with several instances per resource · What the Banker’s algorithm needs, and its limits · Implement the safety and request algorithms

modules.name: Lab 6 — A deadlock-avoiding resource manager
modules.description: Luyện: A deadlock-avoiding resource manager

modules.name: 7.1 Essential Linux commands
modules.description: Luyện: Commands, redirection and pipes (concepts) · Predict the output of the pipeline · Read an ls -l line · Redirection order, jobs and signals · Implement chmod with symbolic modes

modules.name: 7.2 Shell scripting basics
modules.description: Luyện: Variables, quoting and special parameters · Predict the output of the one-liner · Exit codes and && / || chains · Split a command line into words like the shell · Subshells, pipelines, jobs and trap

modules.name: 8.1 Multiple processor systems: UMA/NUMA, Amdahl, networks
modules.description: Luyện: UMA, NUMA, spin locks and scheduling (concepts) · Speed-up and parallel efficiency · The omega network: stages and switches

modules.name: 9.1 Security: principles, entropy, ACLs and capabilities
modules.description: Luyện: Principles, attacks and defences (concepts) · Password entropy · From the access matrix to ACLs and capability lists

modules.name: PE Practice — FE mock exams (3 × 15 questions, timed)
modules.description: Luyện: Introduction, processes, scheduling and memory (15 questions) · File systems, I/O and deadlock (15 questions) · Mixed paper with Linux, security and virtualization (15 questions)

modules.name: 14.3 CS.3 Thread pools & Little’s law
modules.description: Luyện: How many worker threads? · Little’s law and pool sizing in code

modules.name: 14.5 CS.5 Memory on a real server: RSS, OOM and exit codes
modules.description: Luyện: Resident memory, overcommit and the OOM killer · Decode the exit code 128 + n · Write an exit-code explainer
